title: Permutations of a String with Duplicates
statement:
Given a string `s` of lowercase letters, print every distinct arrangement of its characters. The string may contain repeated letters, so different orderings of identical letters give the same arrangement, which must be printed only once. If all letters are different this is simply every permutation of the string.

Print the arrangements in lexicographic (dictionary) order, one per line.

**Follow-up:** Explain your algorithm by drawing the recursion tree for a small input such as `aab` and show where duplicate branches are pruned. Then, for a number given as digits, find only its next lexicographically larger permutation (the next-permutation problem) without generating all of them.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print every distinct permutation of `s` in lexicographic order, one per line.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

examples.output:
abc
acb
bac
bca
cab
cba
examples.explanation: All letters are different, so there are 3! = 6 arrangements, listed in dictionary order.
Only 3 distinct arrangements exist: the two `a` letters are interchangeable, so `aab`, `aba` and `baa` each appear once instead of twice.

complexity.time: O(n · P), where P is the number of distinct permutations (at most n!)

hints: Plain backtracking that swaps or picks characters produces duplicates when letters repeat. Think about how to avoid choosing the same letter twice at the same position.
Count the letters (or sort them) and, at each position of the permutation, try each distinct letter at most once.
If you iterate over the distinct letters in alphabetical order, the permutations come out already in lexicographic order, so no final sorting or set is needed.
